summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old man with alcoholic cirrhosis and chronic steroid-dependent asthma was admitted for weakness, shortness of breath, and abdominal pain after resuming alcohol use. He was treated for alcohol withdrawal with CIWA protocol, thiamine, and folate. His respiratory symptoms were attributed to a severe asthma exacerbation, managed with high-dose steroids, nebulizers, and oxygen, with gradual improvement. Elevated beta glucan and pulmonary nodules on CT prompted concern for PCP or fungal infection; he was started on Bactrim prophylaxis and underwent a CT-guided lung biopsy, which revealed scar tissue. An EGD showed esophageal candidiasis, treated with fluconazole. Liver imaging showed stable cirrhosis without HCC but worsening portal hypertension. He was discharged on a prednisone taper, fluconazole, Bactrim, and liver support medications, with follow-up arranged in pulmonology, hepatology, and primary care.
